title: Central bank gold statistics: June 2026
gist: World Gold Council's June 2026 reserve tally shows publicly reported central bank gold buying still led by Poland (82t y-t-d), Uzbekistan (41t), China (40t) and Kazakhstan (27t), while Turkey (83t) and Russia (44t) are the dominant sellers — leaving named buyers roughly 104t ahead of named sellers. Turkey's selling was front-loaded into Q1 and collapsed to just 4t in Q2, and the note flags that these figures capture only publicly reported changes, excluding the unreported buying that inflates the WGC's own Gold Demand Trends series. The raw record carries no published_date field; the article itself is dated 4 August, 2026.

themes.theme: Poland's outsized lead in official buying

insights.claim: Poland is the largest publicly reported central bank gold buyer of H1 2026 at 82 tonnes year-to-date, roughly double the next-largest buyer, per World Gold Council data through June 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A single European EM buyer absorbing ~80t a half-year is a persistent, price-insensitive bid; watch NBP monthly reserve prints for any pause, which would remove the single biggest visible official buyer.
insights.quote: Poland remains the top buyer (82t), followed by Uzbekistan (41t), China (40t) and Kazakhstan (27t)

insights.claim: Publicly reported H1 2026 central bank gold purchases are concentrated in four countries — Poland 82t, Uzbekistan 41t, China 40t, Kazakhstan 27t — which together account for the large majority of disclosed buying.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Official gold demand is a concentrated, not broad-based, bid — the marginal price impact depends on a handful of identifiable reserve managers rather than a diffuse trend.

insights.claim: China's People's Bank added 40 tonnes of gold in publicly reported terms during H1 2026, placing it third behind Poland and Uzbekistan rather than leading global official accumulation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Positions built on a narrative of China as the dominant gold buyer are mis-sized against the disclosed data; Poland is the bigger visible flow.

themes.theme: Turkey and Russia as the offsetting sell side

insights.claim: Turkey is the largest year-to-date official gold seller of 2026 at 83 tonnes, with the selling concentrated in Q1 rather than spread across the half-year.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
entities: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey
insights.so_what: Turkish selling has been the main visible offset to EM buying; because it was front-loaded, the H1 net figure understates the current run-rate of official accumulation.
insights.quote: Turkey remains the largest y-t-d seller (83t) with most of its selling activity concentrated in Q1.

insights.claim: Turkish official gold sales collapsed to just 4 tonnes in Q2 2026 from a Q1-dominated 83t year-to-date total, with a reduction in gold swaps recorded at the end of June.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The largest seller has effectively stepped aside; if Turkey stays out, net official demand mechanically improves in H2 without any new buyer emerging.
insights.quote: Sales in Q2 were a modest 4t with reduction in swaps recorded at the end of June.
insights.locator: Turkey remains the largest y-t-d seller

insights.claim: Russia was a net seller of 44 tonnes of gold year-to-date through June 2026, making it the second-largest official seller after Turkey.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A sanctioned reserve manager liquidating gold cuts against the 'sanctions drive gold accumulation' narrative and signals reserves are being drawn on for fiscal or FX needs.
insights.quote: Russia also sold gold, with 44t net sales y-t-d.

insights.claim: Summing the countries named in the June 2026 World Gold Council note, publicly reported buying of roughly 231 tonnes (Poland 82, Uzbekistan 41, China 40, Kazakhstan 27, Czech Republic 11, Singapore 10, Chile 8, Jordan 6, Ghana 6) exceeds named selling of 127 tonnes (Turkey 83, Russia 44) for a net of about +104 tonnes in H1 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Headline official gold demand looks far weaker on a disclosed-net basis than gross buying suggests — the two big sellers absorb over half of the visible bid.

insights.claim: A second tier of smaller official buyers added meaningful gold in H1 2026 — Czech Republic 11t, Singapore 10t, Chile 8t, Jordan 6t and Ghana 6t — spanning Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The buyer base is geographically broad, so official demand is unlikely to vanish on any single country's policy shift even though tonnage is concentrated.
insights.quote: Other major net buyers include Czech Republic (11t), Singapore (10t), Chile (8t), Jordan (6t) and Ghana (6t).

insights.claim: Beyond the named names, the residual central bank gold buyers in H1 2026 are diversified across emerging markets rather than concentrated in developed-market reserve managers.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Structural EM reserve diversification into gold remains intact and is the durable component of official demand, distinct from episodic large-buyer activity.
insights.quote: Other smaller buyers are diversified within the emerging markets.

themes.theme: Reported vs. estimated demand — the data caveat

insights.claim: The World Gold Council's monthly central bank statistics count only publicly reported reserve changes, whereas its Gold Demand Trends series adds an estimate for unreported buying — so the monthly country tallies systematically understate true official demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Never compare the monthly country table to the quarterly Gold Demand Trends headline; the gap between them is itself the estimate of covert official buying and is the number to track.
insights.quote: Central bank demand presented here comprises consist solely of publicly reported changes. This differs from our Gold Demand Trend statistics, which consist of aggregate reported changes as well as an estimate for unreported buying.

insights.claim: The country and year-to-date breakdowns in this dataset include only reserve changes of one tonne or more, and exclude Azerbaijan's State Oil Fund (SOFAZ), which reports quarterly rather than monthly.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Sub-tonne accumulation across many small reserve managers is invisible in this table, so the count of participating buyers is a floor, not a full census.
insights.quote: By country and y-t-d charts include changes of one tonne or more only.
